artworks.title: Themis of Rhamnous
artworks.description: Marble cult statue of Themis sculpted by Chairestratos, discovered in the goddess's small temple at Rhamnous in Attica and now in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens. The goddess of divine law and right order stands draped in chiton and himation, her base preserving the sculptor's signature.

artworks.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha Praying before the Statue of Themis
artworks.description: Tintoretto's flood survivors kneel before the cult image of Themis — the goddess of right counsel who tells them to cast their mother's bones (the stones of Earth) behind them and remake humankind.

artworks.title: Allegory of Justice – Themis
artworks.description: Bacciarelli's Warsaw allegory: Themis as Justice with scales and sword — divine order translated into the Enlightenment courtroom's emblem.

artworks.title: Themis
artworks.description: Another Bacciarelli Themis from the Polish royal cycle: the titaness of sacred custom enthroned as law's personification — scales, gaze, and classical drapery for a modern throne room.

popCulture.title: Lady Justice
popCulture.description: Courthouse statues of blindfolded Justice descend from Themis and her Roman heir Justitia — divine order turned into the scales of law.

popCulture.title: Themis
popCulture.description: Legal and philosophical English still reaches for Themis when it needs a name for sacred custom and right order older than statute.
